text:
Maya Patel: quick idea — want to test an experiment for 2 weeks: when a Sev2+ incident channel moves to `resolved` and the incident tag is set, have a bot auto-create a postmortem skeleton (summary, timeline, impact, initial action items) and ping the handoff rotation. aim is to cut the friction of scheduling and reduce missing follow-ups. low risk canary first. anyone object?

Ash Chen: +1 from me. main risk is duplicate docs and ownership confusion. how does the bot pick the assignee? we need to avoid a ping to an empty rotation.

Devon Ortiz: agree with Ash. also please include customer-impact snippet and any customer-facing notes. those are the things that often get delayed. can the bot pull customer IDs from the incident metadata?

Maya Patel: plan is: bot creates doc in the Postmortems space named `INC-<id> - auto-skeleton` and sets assignee to `@hand-off` rotation (falls back to oncall lead if empty). it will copy incident header and timeline summary. manual step: someone should claim and expand. canary: run on one low-risk Sev2 this week only.

Luca Marino: :thumbsup: for canary. suggestion: attach a short checklist that includes a forced "confirm customer impact" and "confirm action owner" step. otherwise people skip.

Ash Chen: a checklist is good. also we should emit an event to the action dashboard so that created action items are tracked automatically. otherwise they sit in the doc and nobody sees them.

postmortem-bot: :robot_face: scheduled run: canary enabled. will create skeletons for incidents with severity >= 2 and tag `postmortem-auto`. template: `skeleton_v2`. fallback assignee: rotation `oncall-handoff`. will set due_date = now + 72h.

Devon Ortiz: can you show the skeleton structure? want to vet fields we need to capture so the dashboard can ingest them.

postmortem-bot: sure — example skeleton (created content):

```
Title: INC-2026-12345 - auto-skeleton
Summary: short summary pulled from incident header
Timeline: || placeholder ||
Customer Impact: | customers | severity | notes |
Immediate Mitigation: bullet list
Action Items: - [ ] owner: @ — description — due: yyyy-mm-dd
Root Cause: placeholder
Postmortem Owner: @hand-off (to claim)
```

Luca Marino: the Action Items format above is parseable — good. add a mandatory `Action ID` prefix (e.g., AM-<inc>-1) so the action dashboard can index items uniquely across docs.

Ash Chen: question: how do we avoid creating a skeleton if someone already made a draft? maybe check docs with title prefix or an embed flag in the incident thread. the bot should be idempotent.

postmortem-bot: plan: before creating, check for any doc titled `INC-<id>` in Postmortems space. if exists and last updated < 10 minutes ago, skip. also check for `postmortem:draft=true` flag in incident header metadata.

Maya Patel: good. also add an audit trail line in the incident channel so SRE can see that a skeleton was auto-created: `postmortem-bot created INC-2026-12345 (auto-skeleton) — assigned to @hand-off — due in 72h`. that helps reviews and handoffs.

Devon Ortiz: and send a webhook to the action-dashboard service: payload includes incident_id, doc_url, actions[] (if any), customers[]. we can use this to populate the dashboard and alert if actions become stale after 7d.

Ash Chen: one more ops concern: retention and PII. ensure the bot strips any raw logs or full customer PII from the automatic skeleton. only include high-level impact and references to logs. we should add a quick review step that flags PII before publishing.

postmortem-bot: will redact fields matching regex `/customer_id|email|phone/` and add a `PII_REVIEW_REQUIRED` tag if redactions occurred. final publish will be gated until claimed by a human with `owner` role.

Luca Marino: sounds sensible. for the canary: pick an incident this week and have the bot create skeleton but do not publish publicly, only put it in a private Postmortems draft folder so we can review.

Maya Patel: agreed. action items from this thread:
- Maya -> flip canary on for one incident, private draft (due: today EOD)
- Ash -> add Action ID prefixing & webhook spec for action-dashboard (due: 2d)
- Devon -> verify incident metadata contains customer IDs and propose schema (due: 2d)
- Luca -> add checklist items and PII gating rules to template (due: 2d)

Ash Chen: tagging @sre-bot to remind us to follow up on the 2d items.

sre-bot: reminder set: follow-up in 48h (will post status in #eng-sre).

Maya Patel: thanks everyone. i'll post the canary details in #incidents and ping oncall for the chosen incident. if the canary looks good we'll flip to opt-in for all Sev2+ after a week.

Devon Ortiz: lgtm. please make sure the bot's audit logs include the user who requested creation so we have traceability.

Maya Patel: yep — bot will include `created_by:user` (user is the person who closed or tagged the incident). final note: if anyone has concerns about noisy pings, we can change the default to only post in the incident channel and not ping the whole rotation. canary will use no pings.

Ash Chen: perfect. let's reconvene after canary results. :heavy_check_mark:
